html:
Somalia is a country in the Horn of Africa, with the longest coastline on the African mainland. The map shows it in 1815 and again from 1945, when it covers the lands of the Somali people along the coast.

Somali towns such as Mogadishu, Zeila and Berbera were trading ports for centuries.

In the late 1800s the Somali lands were split five ways: British Somaliland in the north, Italian Somaliland in the south, French Somaliland (now Djibouti), the Ogaden under Ethiopia, and northern Kenya under Britain. The Dervish leader Mohammed Abdullah Hassan fought the British and Italians for twenty years.

The British and Italian parts united as an independent Somali Republic on 1 July 1960. In 1969 General Siad Barre seized power. His attempt to take the Ogaden from Ethiopia in 1977 and 1978 failed, and his regime grew more brutal until it collapsed in 1991.

The state then fell apart. Clan militias fought over Mogadishu, and Somaliland in the north declared itself independent. Islamist groups, including al-Shabaab, fought a weak federal government from the 2000s. A large Somali diaspora keeps the economy going with money sent home.
